content:
#11 I have added a new section, “In homotopy type theory”, between the existing homotopy theory and cohesive ∞-topos sections.

In this section, I describe monodromy in terms of transport in dependent type families, including fiber self-equivalences, compatibility with path composition, and induced equivalences on higher homotopy groups.

I refer to the HoTT Book (§§2.3 and 4.8) and distinguish transport-based monodromy from the additional structure required to obtain an action on fixed-basepoint homotopy groups.

I am also working on a corresponding Cubical Agda formalization, which I plan to link here after completing the mathematical and semantic review.

Hongwei Wang

#12 I have refined the new homotopy type theory section to make the mathematical constructions and their relationships more explicit.

In particular, I added a homotopy pullback diagram for the type-family representation of fibrations, a homotopy-commutative diagram for the composition of transport maps, and a more precise discussion of the change-of-basepoint issue for higher homotopy groups.

I also improved the exposition and corrected unresolved internal links.

Hongwei Wang

#13 I have refined the exposition in the “In homotopy type theory” section to better follow the mathematical writing style of the nLab.

In particular, I have made the discussion more concise, reduced unnecessary displayed equations, and improved the transitions between type families, transport, and monodromy.

I have also added internal links to relevant nLab concepts while preserving the homotopy pullback and transport-composition diagrams.

The discussion of induced homotopy-group isomorphisms and the change-of-basepoint issue has been retained for mathematical clarity.

Hongwei Wang
